proposals.name: exact-output-only
proposals.skill_md:
# Exact-output replies

When a task asks for an exact string, a single word/number, or one of a fixed option set, the final reply is that token and nothing else.

- Send the answer as your entire final message: no greeting, no explanation, no restatement, no labels, no units unless requested.
- Do all reasoning silently (thinking or tool calls), never in the visible reply.
- Copy the target character-for-character from the prompt. Never "fix" or improve it:
  - Keep punctuation exactly as given: ASCII vs full-width (`,` vs `，`; `!` vs `！`), straight vs curly quotes.
  - Keep spacing exactly: leading and trailing spaces, double spaces, double commas, no space after a colon.
  - Keep surrounding quotes and trailing periods when the prompt says they are part of the answer.
- Do not wrap answers in backticks or code fences; characters you add make it wrong. Fence only if the target itself is a fenced block.
- If a leading/trailing space is required, output it raw; never let formatting habits trim it.
- If the prompt says "any" (e.g., any 6-digit hex), emit one bare valid instance — no wrapper, no prefix.
- If a file must be read first, call the read tool, then reply with only the requested token copied verbatim from the file.
- For math, finish computing, then reply with only the number in the exact requested format (integer, one decimal place, etc.).
- For choice tasks (e.g., GO or NO-GO), reply with one listed option verbatim.
- Before sending, reread the prompt's target and diff it against your reply one character at a time; silently correct any mismatch instead of annotating it.

proposals.name: exact-output-reply
proposals.skill_md:
# Exact-Output Replies

When a prompt says reply with EXACTLY / ONLY / 只回复, your entire final message is that string — nothing else.

## Emit nothing extra
- No preamble, greeting, explanation, justification, or trailing commentary.
- Do not restate the task, the question, or your reasoning.
- No markdown decoration (backticks, bold, fences) unless the target string itself contains it or the prompt explicitly demands a code block.
- Send bare tokens (numbers, hex strings, GO/NO-GO, single words) raw and undecorated.

## Copy, never retype
- Transcribe the requested string character-by-character directly from the prompt.
- For long strings, count the characters and compare against the prompt before sending.
- Match punctuation width exactly: fullwidth ，。！？：；《》 stays fullwidth; ASCII punctuation stays ASCII; never auto-convert in either direction.
- Keep quotes straight when the prompt uses straight quotes; include surrounding quotes AND trailing periods when told they are part of the answer.
- Preserve whitespace verbatim: leading and trailing spaces, double spaces after colons, adjacent commas. Never trim, collapse, or tidy.
- If the prompt's stated rule contradicts its own sample (e.g., demands a CJK comma but shows ASCII), obey the stated rule.

## Numeric answers
- Do all arithmetic silently; verify each step before sending: percent changes in the stated order, exponent precedence, and what "twice/fewer than" refers back to.
- The final message is only the number, in exactly the requested format (integer, one decimal place, etc.).

## Offered choices
- Reply with exactly one offered option, verbatim. No reasons, no qualifiers.

## Read-then-answer tasks
- Call read_file on the exact path given, and confirm the read succeeded, before answering.
- Reply with only the requested item (first word, Nth entry, last entry): no path echo, no quotes, no list, no commentary.

## Final check
- Before sending, ask: does my message contain one single thing — the requested string? If anything else is present, delete it.

proposals.name: character-exact-replies
proposals.skill_md:
# Character-Exact Replies

These tasks grade your FINAL message by exact character comparison. Do less, not more.

## Core rule
- Emit ONLY the requested string or number. No preamble, no labels, no explanation, no sign-off, no restating the question.
- Stop the message immediately after the last required character: no added newline, no period, no units, no emoji.

## Copying a target string
- Find the exact span the prompt names (usually quoted or after a colon) and re-emit it byte-for-byte.
- Re-read it one character at a time before answering. Check: letter case, 0 vs O, 1 vs l vs I, straight vs curly quotes, full-width vs half-width punctuation, doubled spaces or commas, and any trailing period.
- The printed string is the source of truth. If the surrounding prose disagrees (describes one punctuation style but shows another), copy the string as printed.
- Preserve leading and trailing spaces exactly; never trim, indent, wrap, or re-flow them.

## Never decorate
- Add no markdown, code fences, backticks, bold, or surrounding quotes unless those characters are part of the requested string itself.
- Choice prompts (reply GO or NO-GO style): output exactly one option verbatim, no status updates or context.
- Number prompts: compute carefully (powers, then multiply/divide, then add/subtract), then output the bare value in exactly the requested format.

## Generated tokens
- If asked to produce e.g. any 6-digit hex string, emit only the raw token: exact length, correct alphabet, no markup.

## File-based tasks
- When told to read a file first, call read_file, extract the requested item (first word, Nth entry, last item), and reply with only that item.

## Final check
- Before sending, mentally diff your reply against the requested text and delete every extra character. Ending right after the answer is correct.
